prayerExcerpt.en-US: The disciples of the apostles, by assiduous meditation on heavenly things, were so swallowed up in the life to come, that they seemed no longer inhabitants of this world.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Os discípulos dos apóstolos, pela assídua meditação nas coisas celestiais, estavam tão absortos na vida futura que pareciam já não ser habitantes deste mundo.

meta.face: A Greek of Jewish family from Bethlehem, about sixty-five, with a warm, olive-bronze complexion and a face DOMINATED by a LARGE, STRONGLY ARCHED, high-bridged nose — a LOW forehead under a WIDOW'S PEAK of thick, WAVY grey hair brushed back and still full, HOODED, dark-brown eyes that SLANT DOWN at the outer corners under thick, level, black-and-grey brows, HIGH cheekbones over LEAN cheeks, a deep groove above a thin-lipped mouth, a NARROW chin; a MEDIUM, black-and-grey beard cut SQUARE across the bottom; the gaze inward and grave. Not the round, bald, crisp-bearded mark_pope, the tall, egg-shaped anicetus, the soft, heart-shaped soter, the hexagonal linus, the bony, two-pointed cletus, the diamond-faced clement_i or the long, narrow sylvester.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; the Sistine Chapel portrait (Wikipedia's lead image) and the medallion of St. Paul Outside the Walls are late and conventional. The card takes the Liber Pontificalis's Greek of Jewish family from Bethlehem (via Wikipedia) and gives him a Levantine face, bareheaded in first-century dress, on the Vatican hill, where the book says he was buried near St. Peter.
